questions.q: How is manual lineage documentation typically produced?
options: Written by hand by someone who understands the pipeline — a diagram, wiki page, or mapping spreadsheet
Automatically generated by scanning SQL execution logs
Downloaded directly from the source system's vendor
Generated exclusively by AI image models
questions.explain: Manual lineage is the fastest way to get started precisely because it requires no tooling — just someone writing down what they know.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say manual lineage tends to decay over time?
options: Because nothing updates it automatically, and updating it after every pipeline change is easy to skip under deadline pressure
Because manual documentation is deleted by most systems after 30 days
Because manual lineage can only describe one dataset at a time
Because written documentation cannot describe transformations
questions.explain: A hand-drawn diagram is accurate the day it's made but reflects nothing automatically afterward — keeping it current requires active, ongoing upkeep.

questions.q: How does automated lineage generate its dependency graph?
options: By scanning actual pipeline code, SQL queries, or execution logs to infer what feeds what
By asking each team member to fill out a survey
By randomly sampling rows from each table
By copying whatever a manual diagram already says
questions.explain: A tool that parses SQL SELECT and JOIN clauses, for example, can infer that one table depends on another directly from the code, without a human typing the relationship in.

questions.q: What is the main blind spot of automated lineage, according to this lesson?
options: It only sees dependencies expressed in code or logs it can parse — manual steps like an emailed Excel export are invisible to it
It cannot be re-run after a code change
It is always less accurate than manual documentation for every type of dependency
It cannot show direction of data flow
questions.explain: A manual export, a one-off script, or a copy-paste into another system doesn't show up in a code or log scan, because none of it is parseable by the tool.

questions.q: What approach does this lesson say most mature lineage practices actually land on?
options: A hybrid: automated lineage as the backbone for parseable pipeline code, plus manual documentation to fill the gaps automation can't reach
Exclusively manual documentation, since automation is never worth the investment
Exclusively automated lineage, since manual documentation is never useful
No lineage documentation at all, relying entirely on institutional memory
questions.explain: Neither approach alone solves the whole problem — automation covers what it can scan, and manual documentation covers the tribal-knowledge and off-pipeline steps it can't.
